# verify-claims

> A gate for published numbers. Each claim in a repository's `claims.json` either carries a
> command that recomputes the number from committed data, or a written reason why no command
> can — and CI fails when a number stops reproducing. It runs on the Python standard library
> alone, as a CLI or as a GitHub Action.

## Start here

- What it is and how to adopt it: https://github.com/alloevil/verify-claims/blob/main/README.md
- The claims format: README § "The format"; real examples in `example/claims.json`
- The GitHub Action: https://github.com/alloevil/verify-claims/blob/main/action.yml

## What it found

- `docs/measurement.md` — an audit of every public repository of this account, claim by claim,
  against the artefacts each repository commits: how many published claims did not stand up, the
  six failure modes behind them, and the checks the author got wrong while writing it.
- `docs/case-studies.md` — the same failures as individual cases, each with the commit that fixed it.
- `docs/index.md` — every guarded repository and how many of its claims are machine-checked.

## Two commands the gate does not replace

- `verify-claims coverage` lists figures a README publishes that no claim mentions: the gate only
  defends numbers somebody wrote down.
- `verify-claims index` renders the portfolio page above from each repository's own claims file.
